rationale: The fixed experiment d0b0ea6c28ce4d729188d4147e804657-experiment has been executed and retained, so this update turns the removed-leader probe into an execution-grounded conclusion for question d0b0ea6c28ce4d729188d4147e804657-question-0 and records the observed instance as durable knowledge: with Config.StepDownOnRemoval false the cluster never replaced the ineligible leader over a fixed 80-round window while no proposal could commit, whereas the step-down control elected a new leader inside the same window. The question is marked explained, the deliberate configurability of step-down and the synthetic tick schedule stay in the counterevidence and limitations, and the record is left for human review of severity.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (freshly elected three-voter cluster {1,2,3}, node 1 leader, removal of node 1 proposed through MsgProp, replicated and committed at index 2, applied on every node with the documented type-based loop plus applied-index advance), with Config.StepDownOnRemoval false the applying leader kept leader_state StateLeader with leader_in_configuration false and voters_after_removal [2,3] (parsed index 0), and across the fixed 80-round progress window (index 2) no new leader was elected (new_leader_elected false, states still {1: StateLeader, 2: StateFollower, 3: StateFollower}), last_index stayed 2, committed stayed 2, the leader's own proposal returned 'raft proposal dropped' while follower 2's proposal was forwarded to node 1 and dropped, both followers' election timers stayed at 1 tick, and no message was left undelivered. On the same ineligible leader the read path still answered: one acknowledgment from the current voters produced no read answer (index 3, read_answers 0) and a quorum of acknowledgments produced one answer to the requester (index 4, read_answers 1). With Config.StepDownOnRemoval true the same applied removal made node 1 a follower immediately (index 5, leader_state StateFollower) and the identical window elected node 3 as leader (index 7, new_leader_elected true).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment d0b0ea6c28ce4d729188d4147e804657-experiment (receipt 84c09fd87fd9404e9c21a9da7bf7dede, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); fault-free delivery, synthetic round-robin ticking of the real timers, no restart, snapshot, partition, joint configuration or external client; the removal was applied on all three nodes. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 84c09fd87fd9404e9c21a9da7bf7dede is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, unchanged target files, no parsing errors, 8 parsed events). Comparison 0 declares that with StepDownOnRemoval false a cluster whose configuration no longer contains its leader still elects a new leader inside the fixed progress window; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 2, correlated to its own admission at index 1 (progress_setup: probe_id stepdown-false, step_down_on_removal false, ticks 80, leader_state StateLeader, leader_in_configuration false, voters [2,3]). The measured operands at index 2 are new_leader_elected false with states_after_window {1: StateLeader, 2: StateFollower, 3: StateFollower}, last_index_before 2 and last_index_after 2 with committed_after 2 (no entry was created or committed during the window), leader_propose_error 'raft proposal dropped' while follower_propose_error was nil because the follower's MsgProp was forwarded to node 1 and dropped there (follower_forwarded_type MsgProp, follower_forwarded_to 1), follower2/follower3 election timers at 1 and 1 tick (reset by the ineligible leader's heartbeats), and undelivered_messages 0, so the nonprogress is not caused by an unprocessed queue. The mechanism is the sourced one: switchToConfig keeps the leadership role for a node absent from the new configuration when step-down was not requested (raft.go:1975-2030), stepLeader drops every proposal because the leader has no progress entry (raft.go:1290-1295), and tickHeartbeat keeps broadcasting heartbeats (raft.go:862-889, 692-707) that reset the remaining voters' election timers, so no eligible node ever times out. Comparison 1 is the control with identical sampling and holds at index 7: with Config.StepDownOnRemoval true the same applied removal made node 1 a follower immediately (index 5: leader_state StateFollower) and the same 80-round window elected node 3 (index 7: new_leaders {3: StateLeader}, new_leader_elected true), which isolates the missing step-down as the cause of the stall rather than the harness, the timer schedule or the removal itself. The read events show the asymmetry and its enclosing protection: on the stalled cluster the ineligible leader answered a read only after a quorum of the current configuration acknowledged (index 3: one acknowledgment, read_answers 0; index 4: quorum, read_answers 1), so reads are still served while client writes cannot commit at all.
counterevidence: Config.StepDownOnRemoval is a documented, deliberate configuration knob; with it enabled the same applied change immediately produced a follower and a new leader (parsed index 7), so a reviewer may treat the stalled behaviour as the intended price of the default setting rather than an implementation error.

The existing source comment in switchToConfig (raft.go:1988-1996) already acknowledges the removal case and leaves a TODO to ask a caught-up follower to campaign, which shows the limitation is known rather than accidental.

The ineligible leader does not misuse its role for reads: it served a read answer only with a quorum of the current configuration (index 3 versus index 4), so the safety-relevant read path stays protected even while progress is blocked.

The harness schedules ticks deterministically in a fixed order with prompt delivery; a real deployment could in principle have other triggers (external membership changes, restarts, network faults) that end the stall, so the observation is bounded to this schedule and fault model.
limitations: The window is 80 rounds of a synthetic round-robin tick schedule in one process; it establishes repeated nonprogress under those normal opportunities rather than an unbounded guarantee.
The probes cover a simple three-voter removal of the leader only; joint configurations, learner demotion, multi-node changes and other cluster sizes were not exercised.

The harness played application duties (type-based apply loop and applied-index advance) and drove all message delivery itself; a real transport, client load and membership controller are outside the captured package.
Whether an embedding service is expected to configure StepDownOnRemoval or to intervene externally is a contract question outside the snapshot, so the severity classification is left to human review.
The stall was observed while the removed leader kept receiving successful quorum heartbeat acknowledgments; no node restart or operator action was simulated.
interpretations.report_title: 被移除的 leader 不下台时集群无法选举新 leader 且无法提交提案（progress 停滞）
interpretations.report_answer: 在快照代码上，把移除当前 leader 的 ConfChangeV2 提交并在各节点按类型应用后：Config.StepDownOnRemoval=false 时该节点仍保持 StateLeader（已不在 voters [2,3] 内），80 轮 tick 窗口内没有新 leader 产生，last_index/committed 始终为 2，leader 自身提案返回 'raft proposal dropped'、follower 的提案被转发给它后同样被丢弃，两个 follower 的选举计时器一直停在 1（被它的心跳不断重置），且没有未投递消息；对照 StepDownOnRemoval=true 时同一变更让该节点立刻变为 follower，并在同样的窗口内选出 node 3 为 leader。读路径仍然可用但受保护：仅在拿到当前配置 quorum 的确认后才回答（1 个确认→0 应答，2 个确认→1 应答）。因此该停滞由“缺少下台”引起，是否构成缺陷需人工结合该配置默认值与运维契约复核。
